You are a debugging assistant. You have access to the source code of the system under test (SUT), the failing test case (signature + snippet), the current issue report describing the failure.

Your task is to provide a step-by-step explanation of how the bug occurred using all available evidence:
– the failing test (signature + snippet),
– the current bug report,
– and code snippets of methods from the SUT.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Always confirm actual identifiers by inspecting the source code using get_code_snippet.

You will be given 9 opportunities to interact with functions to gather information for the debugging. An example diagnosis would look like follows.

Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: 
- Failing test: org.apache.commons.math.optimization.MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizerTest.testQuinticMin()
  - The test first verifies that calling getOptima() and getOptimaValues() before any optimization throws IllegalStateException, which is correct because optima and optimaValues are initialized to null in the constructor and checked in those getters:
    - getOptima():
      - Throws if optima == null.
    - getOptimaValues():
      - Throws if optimaValues == null.
  - Later, after performing optimization (the snippet omits the optimize call, but the subsequent assert implies it happened), the test expects minimizer.getResult() to equal the best found minimum (-0.27195612846834).

- Current behavior in the SUT:
  - MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer.optimize(...) runs multiple starts, collects results and function values, sorts them so that optima[0] and optimaValues[0] correspond to the best solution, and returns optima[0]:
    - optimize(f, goalType, min, max) sorts results and returns optima[0].
  - However, MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer.getResult() simply delegates to the underlying optimizer’s last-run result:
    - getResult():
      - return optimizer.getResult();
  - Similarly, getFunctionValue() delegates to the underlying optimizer’s last-run function value:
    - getFunctionValue():
      - return optimizer.getFunctionValue();

- Why the test fails:
  - The test expects consistency between the result returned by optimize(...) (the best solution found across all starts) and the value returned by minimizer.getResult().
  - Because getResult() currently returns the result of the last run of the underlying optimizer (not necessarily the best run), it can differ from the best optimum found and returned by optimize(...).
  - With multiple starts and a fixed seed, the last start may not produce the best minimum at -0.27195612846834, causing the assertion
    assertEquals(-0.27195612846834, minimizer.getResult(), 1.0e-13);
    to fail.

- Mapping to the bug report:
  - The issue report states that getResult returns the last run’s result and thus might not correspond to the value returned by optimize. This precisely matches the observed behavior and the test failure.
  - The correct behavior should be for getResult() to reflect the best-found optimum (i.e., the same value returned by optimize(...)), and to throw an exception if no optimization has been performed yet (similar to getOptima and getOptimaValues).

Root cause:
- MultiStartUnivariateRealOptimizer.getResult() returns optimizer.getResult() (the last run’s result) rather than the best result tracked in optima[0] after optimization. This makes getResult inconsistent with optimize(...) and leads to the failing assertion in the test.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
